questions.question_text: Etiquette differs from manners and protocol in that etiquette is:
options: The accepted code of polite behaviour in a setting, while manners are personal habits of courtesy and protocol is formal rules for official occasions
questions.explanation: Protocol governs state and diplomatic events.

questions.question_text: Business etiquette is:
options: The accepted standards of professional behaviour in the workplace
questions.explanation: It covers greetings, dress, communication and meetings.

questions.question_text: Business etiquette is important because it:
options: Builds professional relationships, trust and a positive image
questions.explanation: It helps careers and company reputation.

questions.question_text: A principle of business etiquette is:
options: Respect, courtesy, punctuality and consideration for others

questions.question_text: A first impression is formed:
options: Within the first few seconds (often cited as about 7 seconds) of meeting
questions.explanation: It is hard to change later.

questions.question_text: In a business setting, one should greet and introduce oneself by:
options: Smiling, making eye contact, offering a handshake and stating name and role clearly

questions.question_text: In introductions, the correct order is to introduce:
options: The junior to the senior and the colleague to the client
questions.explanation: Mention the more important person's name first.

questions.question_text: Business card etiquette is to:
options: Give and receive cards with both hands, read them and keep them respectfully
Write on them in front of the giver
questions.explanation: It is especially important in Japan.

questions.question_text: The right way to address colleagues and clients is:
options: By appropriate titles and surnames until invited to use first names

questions.question_text: The importance of a handshake is that it:
options: Creates a positive first impression; it should be firm, brief and with eye contact

questions.question_text: Positive body language includes:
options: Eye contact, a smile, open posture, nodding and a firm handshake
questions.explanation: Negative gestures include fidgeting and checking the phone.

questions.question_text: Proxemics is:
options: The study of personal space and distance in communication

questions.question_text: In high-context cultures such as Japan and India, communication is:
options: Indirect and relies on context, while low-context cultures like the US and Germany are direct and explicit

questions.question_text: A tip for cross-cultural business etiquette is to:
options: Research the culture, respect customs, be patient and avoid assumptions

questions.question_text: Punctuality differs across cultures in that:
options: Germany and Japan expect strict punctuality, while some cultures are more relaxed about time
questions.explanation: It is best to be on time always.

questions.question_text: A gift-giving etiquette is that in Japan, gifts are:
options: Wrapped neatly and given and received with both hands
questions.explanation: In China avoid clocks; in India avoid giving leather items to Hindus in some settings.

questions.question_text: Email etiquette is:
options: The accepted rules for writing professional emails, including tone, clarity and courtesy
questions.explanation: It includes subject lines, greetings and closings.

questions.question_text: A good subject line is:
options: Clear and specific, e.g., "Meeting request: Project review on 15 Oct"
questions.explanation: It tells the reader the purpose.

questions.question_text: A formal email uses the salutation and closing:
questions.explanation: Use "Dear Sir/Madam," when the name is unknown.

questions.question_text: To, Cc and Bcc differ in that To is for _____, Cc for _____, and Bcc for _____:
options: Main recipients; people to be informed; hidden recipients
questions.explanation: Bcc recipients are not visible to others.

questions.question_text: "Reply all" should be used:
options: Only when everyone on the email needs the reply
questions.explanation: Otherwise reply to the sender only.

questions.question_text: ALL CAPS should be avoided in emails because:
options: It looks like shouting and is rude

questions.question_text: The ideal response time for business emails is:
questions.explanation: Acknowledge sooner if the answer will take time.

questions.question_text: Attachments should be handled by:
options: Naming files clearly, keeping sizes reasonable and mentioning them in the email
questions.explanation: Check that the attachment is included.

questions.question_text: An out-of-office reply is:
options: An automatic message informing senders that you are away and when you will respond
questions.explanation: It may include an alternative contact.

questions.question_text: In email tone, one should avoid:
A suitable opening line for an email requesting a meeting with a client is:
options: "I would like to request a meeting at your convenience to discuss the proposal."

questions.question_text: A suitable opening line apologising for a delivery delay is:
options: "We sincerely apologise for the delay in delivering your order."

questions.question_text: A suitable opening line requesting three days' leave is:
options: "I would like to request leave from 10 to 12 October due to a family function."

questions.question_text: A suitable opening line thanking an interviewer is:
options: "Thank you for taking the time to interview me for the position."

questions.question_text: A suitable opening line requesting a quotation from a vendor is:
options: "Kindly send us a quotation for the supply of 100 office chairs."

questions.question_text: A suitable opening line complaining about a defective product is:
options: "I am writing to inform you that the product I received on 5 October is defective."

questions.question_text: A suitable opening line announcing a team meeting is:
options: "There will be a team meeting on Monday at 10 am in the conference room."
questions.explanation: It gives date, time and place.

questions.question_text: A suitable opening line declining a job offer politely is:
options: "Thank you for the offer; after careful consideration, I regret to decline."

questions.question_text: A professional rewrite of "hey, send me the report asap!!!" is:
options: "Dear Rohan, could you please send me the report by 5 pm today? Thank you."

questions.question_text: An improved subject line for "Hi" is:
questions.explanation: It tells the reader the purpose.

questions.question_text: Netiquette means:
options: Rules of polite and responsible behaviour online, such as being respectful and avoiding spam

questions.question_text: Professional social-media etiquette includes:
options: Keeping posts respectful, avoiding confidential information and protecting your reputation

questions.question_text: Telephone etiquette is:
options: Polite and professional behaviour on phone calls
questions.explanation: It includes greetings, listening and closing.

questions.question_text: A professional phone greeting is:
options: "Good morning, ABC Company. This is Anita speaking. How may I help you?"
questions.explanation: It names the firm and speaker.

questions.question_text: While making a business call, you should:
options: Introduce yourself, state the purpose and ask if it is a convenient time

questions.question_text: To put a caller on hold, you should:
options: Ask permission, explain why and thank them for holding; when transferring, tell them who you are transferring to
questions.explanation: Do not keep them waiting long.

questions.question_text: While taking a message, note:
options: Caller's name, number, time, purpose and the person it is for

questions.question_text: To handle an angry caller:
options: Stay calm, listen, apologise where appropriate and offer a solution

questions.question_text: A call should be closed by:
options: Summarising actions, thanking the caller and saying goodbye politely
questions.explanation: Let the caller end it if possible.

questions.question_text: A suitable line from a receptionist to a visitor wanting to meet the manager is:
options: "May I have your name and the purpose of your visit? I will check if he is available."

questions.question_text: When taking a message for an absent manager, a suitable line is:
options: "Mr Rao is out of the office. May I take a message?"

questions.question_text: Mobile phone etiquette in meetings is to:
options: Switch the phone to silent and avoid using it

questions.question_text: Dining etiquette is:
options: The set of manners to follow while eating, especially at formal and business meals
questions.explanation: It includes table manners and conversation.

questions.question_text: Before a business dinner, one should:
options: Arrive on time, wait for the host to be seated and place the napkin on the lap

questions.question_text: At a formal table, cutlery is used:
options: From the outside in, with the fork on the left and the knife on the right
questions.explanation: Dessert cutlery is placed above the plate.

questions.question_text: BMW in table setting means:
questions.explanation: It helps remember where things are.

questions.question_text: Napkin and bread plate etiquette: the napkin goes _____ and the bread plate is on the _____:
At a business lunch, one should order:
Topics to avoid during a business meal include:
In a business meal, the bill is paid by:
questions.explanation: The guest should thank the host.

questions.question_text: To signal that you have finished eating, you should:
options: Place the knife and fork together on the plate (parallel, like 4 o'clock)
questions.explanation: The waiter understands you are done.

questions.question_text: In an Indian professional dining setting, it is polite to:
options: Wash hands, wait for elders to start and respect dietary preferences
Use the left hand for eating always
questions.explanation: The right hand is used where customary.

questions.question_text: Alcohol etiquette in business is to:
options: Drink moderately or decline politely, and never pressurise others

questions.question_text: An office etiquette rule is to:
options: Be punctual, respect colleagues' time and keep the workplace tidy
questions.explanation: Also dress appropriately and use shared items carefully.

questions.question_text: Punctuality in the office shows:
The best way to deal with office gossip is to:
options: Avoid participating and not spread rumours

questions.question_text: The POSH Act is:
options: The Prevention of Sexual Harassment at Workplace Act, 2013

questions.question_text: Cubicle etiquette is:
options: Keeping noise low and respecting neighbours' space

questions.question_text: An open-plan office rule is to:
options: Keep your voice down, use headphones and avoid strong smells

questions.question_text: In a cubicle, phone calls should be:
options: Taken quietly or in a meeting room

questions.question_text: To respect others' privacy in a shared workspace, you should:
options: Not read others' screens or papers and knock before entering

questions.question_text: Types of dress code include:
options: Business formal, business casual, smart casual and casual

questions.question_text: Business formal attire is:
options: A suit with a tie or formal Indian wear, polished shoes and neat grooming
questions.explanation: It is used in conservative settings.

questions.question_text: Business casual is:
options: Smart but relaxed clothing like trousers and a collared shirt without a tie

questions.question_text: For interview attire, choose:
options: Clean, well-fitted, conservative clothes appropriate to the company
questions.explanation: When unsure, dress slightly more formally.

questions.question_text: For video calls, dress:
options: Professionally from head to toe and have a neat background
questions.explanation: Treat it like an in-person meeting.

questions.question_text: In office dressing, avoid:
options: Clothes that are too revealing, wrinkled, dirty or with offensive slogans

questions.question_text: Dress influences perception because:
options: People judge competence and professionalism partly by appearance

questions.question_text: Meeting etiquette is:
options: Polite behaviour before, during and after a meeting

questions.question_text: To prepare for a meeting, you should:
options: Read the agenda, prepare points and arrive on time

questions.question_text: An agenda is:
options: A list of topics to be discussed at a meeting with time and place

questions.question_text: During a meeting, one should:
options: Listen actively, speak when appropriate and avoid interrupting

questions.question_text: The role of the chairperson is to:
options: Conduct the meeting, keep to the agenda and ensure everyone gets a chance to speak

questions.question_text: Minutes of a meeting are:
options: A written record of the discussion and decisions of a meeting
questions.explanation: They contain date, attendees, items and decisions.

questions.question_text: Minutes should include:
options: Date, time, place, attendees, decisions and action items
questions.explanation: They should be concise and accurate.

questions.question_text: An agenda for a staff meeting typically includes:
options: Call to order, minutes of the last meeting, agenda items and any other business
questions.explanation: It ends with the next meeting date.

questions.question_text: Virtual meeting etiquette includes:
options: Joining on time, muting when not speaking and using the camera appropriately

questions.question_text: A quorum is:
options: The minimum number of members required to hold a valid meeting
questions.explanation: Without it, decisions may not be valid.

questions.question_text: To disagree politely in a meeting, say:
options: "I see it differently; may I share another perspective?"

questions.question_text: To handle interruptions in a meeting, one should:
options: Politely ask to finish the point or defer questions to the end

questions.question_text: Lift etiquette is to:
options: Let people exit first, press the floor politely and keep conversations quiet

questions.question_text: The etiquette for visiting a client's office is to:
options: Arrive on time, greet the receptionist politely and dress professionally

questions.question_text: The etiquette for hosting a guest is to:
options: Welcome warmly, offer refreshments and make them comfortable

questions.question_text: At networking events, one should:
options: Introduce yourself, listen actively and follow up afterwards

questions.question_text: A thank-you note is important because it:
Criticism should be handled professionally by:
options: Listening calmly, not reacting emotionally and learning from it

questions.question_text: Business travel etiquette includes:
options: Being punctual, respecting local customs and keeping a professional image

questions.question_text: Good etiquette can help your career by:
options: Building trust, relationships and a positive reputation
questions.explanation: People prefer working with courteous colleagues.

questions.question_text: In gift exchange etiquette in business, one should:
options: Follow company policy, choose appropriate modest gifts and avoid anything that looks like a bribe

questions.question_text: The etiquette for a job interview is to:
options: Arrive early, dress well, be polite and prepared, and thank the interviewer

questions.question_text: A suitable line to decline a meeting invitation politely is:
options: "Thank you for the invitation; unfortunately I have a prior commitment and cannot attend."
questions.explanation: It is polite and gives a reason.

questions.question_text: A suitable line to follow up on a pending payment is:
options: "This is a gentle reminder that invoice 123 dated 5 October is yet to be paid."

questions.question_text: A formal email differs from an informal email in that a formal email:
options: Uses polite, standard language and structure, e.g., "Dear Sir", while an informal one is casual, e.g., "Hi Raj"

questions.question_text: A common etiquette mistake made by new employees is:
options: Being late, using phones in meetings or being unfamiliar with norms
questions.explanation: Observe and learn the workplace culture.
